overview: This Senate resolution honors Meriwether Lewis, William Clark, and the Corps of Discovery on the 222nd anniversary of their May 14, 1804, departure from the St. Louis area to explore the land the United States had acquired in the Louisiana Purchase. It praises the expedition's courage and hardship over more than 8,000 miles, its maps and scientific records, and its role in strengthening the young nation's position in North America. It recognizes the help of expedition members including Sacagawea and York, celebrates the expedition's ties to Missouri, and encourages Americans to study its legacy. It is ceremonial and does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors one of the most important journeys of exploration in American history and encourages people to learn about it.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and changes no law, and that its celebration of westward expansion, including its reference to "manifest destiny," gives little attention to the expansion's effects on Native American nations.
